name: Earth
lede: The only world we know with liquid oceans, a protective ozone layer, and a living biosphere — viewed here as NASA's Blue Marble.

landmark.label: Hampton Falls, NH
landmark.blurb: Default observer for the DevConnect Labs sky — Lane family country on the New Hampshire Seacoast.

missions.name: Apollo

missions.name: Landsat
missions.note: Long-running Earth-observation series for land cover and climate.

missions.name: ISS
missions.note: Continuous crewed laboratory in low Earth orbit; visible as a bright moving star.

researchNotes: Earth's axial tilt drives seasons. A roughly 24-hour rotation and a 365.25-day orbit set the calendar used by this planetarium.
The Blue Marble composite shows oceans, clouds, and continents under sunlight. Night lights on companion maps reveal human settlement patterns.
From Hampton Falls, NH — the default sky desk — you can open the full planetarium dome to see tonight's planets and constellations.
folklore: Every culture has origin stories for Earth and sky. On this page we stick to NASA Visible Earth imagery and modern ephemeris.
carlFocus: Treat Earth as home base. Mention Hampton Falls when relevant, seasons from axial tilt, and inviting the visitor into the planetarium dome.
